candidates.observation: Read-only Ghidra analysis of the ELF with SHA-256 53c4a86a8f3dbd7f0d48e440f8607d63c55100aeb364c80d19afefa8097e233a confirms the vtable address point at Ghidra VA 0x1318be60: typeinfo name is 9ItemStack and slot 0 contains 0x086ae038. The entry stores the same vtable pointer through x0, reads state at +0x90, conditionally dispatches through a table using an address at +0x80, then writes 0xffffffff to +0x90 before return. Ghidra records 868 direct call references. Samples pass stack/local addresses in x0: 0x1014749c (x29-0xa8), 0x0fa6a1bc (x23), 0x0f3832bc (sp+0x100), and 0x0f6d8564 (x29-0xc0). Caller function boundaries remain unresolved in this database.
candidates.purpose: Strongly identified ItemStack destruction/cleanup entry from exact RTTI vtable slot and direct-call evidence; not a validated callable engine contract.
candidates.confidence: high for class identity, vtable slot and observed call pattern; medium-high for destructor classification
candidates.ownership_lifetime: Evidence supports cleanup of stack/local ItemStack objects. It does not establish container ownership, copy/move semantics, heap allocation/deallocation, exception behavior, complete object layout, or safe external construction. Ghidra has no usable function/caller boundaries here; decompilation is not trusted.
candidates.abi_assumptions: AArch64 procedure-call convention places the first pointer argument in x0; observed callsites agree. Exact C++ destructor variant, return contract, hidden parameters and C++ runtime compatibility remain unverified.
